themes.consensus_view: Most desks say spending on AI data centers and chips is now the main engine of US stock earnings and keeps running, while a smaller group argues the spending is increasingly paid for with borrowed money and vendor-backed deals that make a bust more likely.

facts_agreed.claim: AI-linked spending and earnings are now the dominant driver of US equity performance.
evidence_quotes: AI infrastructure stocks have accounted for 50% of that EPS growth
it has explained more Russell 1000 index variance than the 1st principal component
AI earnings remain the market's universal solvent with strong outperformance
AI capex is and should continue to be a tailwind for growth.

facts_agreed.claim: Physical infrastructure, hardware and power supply are the binding constraint on AI growth, and that is where the durable demand sits.
evidence_quotes: No. 7 on infrastructure and hardware as the bottleneck
we view today's AI Infrastructure buildout as durable and elongated
hyperscalers will still be incentivized to sign data center PPAs
Own the infrastructure required to produce billions of them.

facts_contested.claim: whether the debt-financed AI buildout is sustainable or is setting up a bust
facts_contested.for_evidence: we view today's AI Infrastructure buildout as durable and elongated
facts_contested.against_evidence: The race to commit early through debt and circular financing also makes a bust more likely.

facts_contested.claim: whether current AI-driven equity valuations are worth owning
facts_contested.for_evidence: our view is that Tech is on its way up
facts_contested.against_evidence: I really don't understand why you should be in the extremely highly valued US stock market.
